cells.tense: You are choosing a direction right now, and the choice is landing from ground you can stand on.
cells.act: hold your shape under the weight
cells.ask: Pick a commitment you are carrying and hold its terms when the days lean on you to stretch or drop them — no defending, no speech, just the line you set.
cells.core:
You can stand back and see how a thing is built — where the pressure comes from, what it feeds — and choose a direction with all of that in view. Reading it and steering it happen in the same breath. That is the difference between being carried and going somewhere, and most days you can tell which one you are doing.

What this week asks is not more push. Fortitude doesn't add force; it keeps shape while weight lands on it. Pick one commitment, and when the days lean on it to stretch or drop, keep the terms you set. No argument, no explaining. Clear direction survives being leaned on, and holding it will tell you fast whether it was yours.

cells.tense: You are pushing ahead of the moment, forcing outcomes that have not arrived yet.
cells.act: draw the whole arrangement you are inside, with yourself marked on it
cells.ask: When you catch yourself forcing a picture to land, stop and sketch everything around the situation — what else shapes it, where you stand on the page. Pencil, once, no fixing it.
cells.core:
You push on the future first and read the situation second. The plan gets built before anyone can say whether it fits, and then the week goes into making the world match a picture you drew by yourself. It works often enough that pushing feels like the method. The strain is the tell.

What brings you back is not less seeing — it is seeing further. Take the situation you have been white-knuckling and put the whole arrangement on paper: what else is holding it up, where you sit inside it. Knowing that keeps deepening can still find its footing. Don't resolve anything. Look. When you stop trying to close the design and start reading it, the ground returns.

cells.tense: You set out with direction once, and the road behind you looks flat now.
cells.act: be what you already are, in your acts
cells.ask: Do an ordinary task in your own manner — your pace, your wording, the version you would know blind — and give nobody a reason for it afterward.
cells.core:
Direction has gone quiet. You still move, and the moves are fine, but it isn't in them the way it used to be. When you look at the day there is no shape you are building toward, and that has stopped reading as something to fix. The question of what you are for comes up flat now, and you answer it without reaching.

Low charge comes back from the other end. Don't try to summon drive. Do one ordinary task exactly as you do it — your tempo, your phrasing, the way only your hands go — and skip the reason afterward. A thing done in your own grain has direction in it before any feeling shows up. Nothing more is asked, and doing it counts.

cells.tense: You are steering your own course, and the name you use for it is drift.
cells.act: do the thing in your own way, without proving it
cells.ask: Take a routine you keep running, do it exactly as you do it — your tempo, your order — and account for nothing. Let your own handling of it stand as the reason.
cells.core:
The steering runs, and you can read patterns well enough to watch it happen — you just don't count it as yours. Pace, order, the way the work went: those read as luck to you, and to anyone watching they read as a course being held by somebody. Nothing is absent. Your name on it is absent.

Try handling one thing under your own flag. Take a routine you have kept going, do it today exactly as you do it — your tempo, your order, the version you would know blind — and account for nothing. Laying your hand on it doesn't make it true; it makes it visible, mostly to you. Balance returns when your own steering stops reading as momentum and starts reading as a call you made.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is in Too Little: I have the person reading their own past as verdict rather than describing the flatness itself, and the record does not say what happened there or how long it has held. A reader could reasonably say the direction has not stopped, they are only tired. The asks all survive a wrong read because each is one act the person can test in an hour or a week without agreeing with the diagnosis. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'There's a wall where the choice used to be' — I have kept it out.
